transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-16 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Solutions); Raj Patel (CTO, Orion), Maya Lin (ML Eng), Ethan Cole (Infra), Lea Ortiz (Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through model trade-offs for our multilingual assistant and document QA product. Orion needs 64k+ context for long docs, and may want 128k in near future. Concern about latency/cost tradeoffs and tool-calling support. Action to run benchmarks on dedicated GPU pool and deliver security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account - with me is Daniel, our SE, and Aisha on solutions. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Raj Patel: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get into this.
[00:12] Maya Lin: Hi - thanks for coming. We put together some prompts and a short repo we'll share after.
[00:18] Daniel Kim: Awesome. Quick agenda - understand your use cases, context length, multilingual needs, tool-calling, then go over model options host/dedicated/private tradeoffs, and propose a benchmark pilot.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: Sound good. For infra background, we run hybrid cloud, mostly GCP, some on-prem for regulated workloads. Network team will ask about VPC peering and private control plane.
[00:40] Lea Ortiz: From security, SOC2 is table stakes; we also need KMS integration and audit logs for anything with PHI or customer PII.

[02:05] Daniel Kim: Great - to the model questions. You mentioned long-doc processing - can you quantify?
[02:12] Maya Lin: We're seeing docs up to 40k tokens now, and roadmap expects multi-doc conversations pushing to 80k-120k. So we need at least 64k, ideally 128k in a year.
[02:25] Daniel Kim: Understood. For context lengths like that, open models vary a lot. Some bleeding-edge shards support 128k but at higher cost and memory. On Redwood we can serve 32k and 64k fairly efficiently on Dedicated; 128k is possible with specialized configs or Private deployments if you want to pin runtime to high-memory GPUs.
[02:44] Raj Patel: What's the perf delta? If we go 128k, latency will blow up?
[02:50] Daniel Kim: There's a tradeoff. Larger context increases memory footprint and per-token compute. You can keep latency reasonable with chunking + KV cache and by using model variants with long-context position encodings. But cost per request goes up. We can mitigate with prefix caching for repeated sections.

[05:10] Sofia Ramirez: Just to add - our Optimize tooling gives batching and quantization suggestions per workload. For long contexts we typically recommend a hybrid: use streaming and KV cache for the conversational head plus short-form summarization to maintain responsiveness.

[06:40] Maya Lin: On models: we prefer open models for auditability; are there Redwood recommendations for specific checkpoints?
[06:48] Daniel Kim: Yes - for multilingual + tool-calling we usually suggest a few families: Mistral-like LLMs for cost/quality balance, and some LL-architectures that have robust instruction-tuning for tool-calling. For 64k contexts, the 32k-extended checkpoints or patched position encodings work well. For 128k, we can run extended context variants but they need more memory and sometimes custom kernels.

[08:22] Ethan Cole: Can you name names? Customers keep asking if it's better to use Anthropic or OpenAI or use open Llama-ish models.
[08:30] Daniel Kim: Sure - competitors that folks evaluate are Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Vertex. For open models we often recommend curated checkpoints from the community with Redwood-verified performance: e.g., variants based on Mistral, LlamaX, and newer long-context forks. We'll share a model perf/cost spreadsheet.

[10:15] Raj Patel: Tool-calling: we need function-calls to our internal search and RDB connectors. Does Redwood support tool-calling across all deployment modes?
[10:25] Aisha Khan: Short answer: yes. We support function/tool calling via structured output and tool invocation hooks. Hosted supports standard tool-calls; Dedicated and Private allow network-level access (VPC) and you can host connectors in your VPC for lower-latency tool calls.
[10:41] Lea Ortiz: For Private, how is KMS handled? We need key material never leaving our VPC.
[10:47] Daniel Kim: Private deployments can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. We provide an optional on-prem package so keys remain under your control. For Dedicated we offer KMS integrations too but keys are customer-managed via supported cloud KMS IAM.

[13:05] Maya Lin: Any runbook for fallback if a model variant fails? We saw in another vendor a panic scenario where fallback caused inconsistent outputs.
[13:15] Daniel Kim: Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We also do canary deploys and A/B rollouts, and per-route model pinning so you can ensure critical paths use the most stable variant. We'll include our rollout playbook in the docs.

[16:30] Raj Patel: Let's talk numbers - how do latency and cost compare across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[16:38] Sofia Ramirez: Hosted is fastest to get going and simplest pricing (usage-based), but you share the multi-tenant infrastructure which can mean slightly variable latency at large scale. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at high volume (reserved GPU pools). Private has the highest setup cost but gives you full control and isolation - good for regulated workloads. We'll send a TCO comparison and a sample pricing sheet.

[19:00] Ethan Cole: For our throughput - we expect 200 reqs/min peak, average 40 reqs/min. Mixed bursty. Any guidance for capacity?
[19:12] Daniel Kim: That fits well with Dedicated. We can provision a baseline pool and autoscale for bursts, or use burst credits. We'll propose a sizing for 2-4 A100-equivalent nodes initially. For on-prem/private, we'll size based on your GPU inventory.

[22:05] Maya Lin: Multilingual - we need parity across English, Spanish, Mandarin, and Portuguese for intent detection and summarization. How do models fare?
[22:16] Daniel Kim: Some open checkpoints are stronger in English and Spanish; Mandarin quality varies. We recommend testing specific prompt sets. Redwood runs eval hooks that report per-language quality degradation and helps pick the best checkpoints. For languages with lower coverage, an instruction-tuned variant or light fine-tune can help.

[25:40] Lea Ortiz: On compliance, SOC2 scope, and auditability - can we get per-token logs or only metadata? We need audit trails without storing PII long-term.
[25:51] Daniel Kim: We provide per-request metadata and full structured audit logs with options for retention policies. For sensitive PII, you can configure redaction and KMS-based encryption for stored traces. We'll share the security pack with specifics.

[28:10] Raj Patel: Ok - objections from procurement: we are sensitive to vendor lock-in. If we go with Redwood Dedicated or Private, how portable are models and tooling?
[28:20] Sofia Ramirez: We design the serving abstraction so you can pin model versions and move to different infra. For Private, it's the customer-managed control plane; we don't lock you into a proprietary model format - models are standard checkpoints and we document conversion steps.

[31:50] Aisha Khan: A quick note on caching: for repeated document headers or knowledge-base context, our KV cache and prefix caching can reduce cost significantly. In one case we saw token cost drop 35% after applying caching profiles.

[33:05] Maya Lin: That sounds promising. For benchmarking, we want to measure latency, 95th percentile, correctness on multilingual test set, and cost per 1k tokens.
[33:16] Daniel Kim: We'll run that. Can you share the prompt set?
[33:20] Maya Lin: I'll upload the repo and docs after this call.

[36:00] Ethan Cole: Network/peering questions - if we do Dedicated, how does VPC peering work?
[36:08] Daniel Kim: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link. For Private deployments we can deploy control plane inside customer VPC or give you an on-prem package. We'll include network diagrams.

[39:45] Raj Patel: Rough timeline - we want a pilot in Q1. If we get good benchmarks we might go Dedicated by mid-Q1. Is that realistic?
[39:54] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, realistic. We'll start with a 2-3 week benchmark phase, then scope a pilot with limited production traffic. We can align RD and solutions on SOW after the benchmarks.

[42:10] Lea Ortiz: One more security question - do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[42:17] Aisha Khan: Yes, SAML/SSO and SCIM are supported on Dedicated and Private; Hosted also supports SSO for enterprise accounts. We'll include the identity integration doc.

[45:00] Daniel Kim: Quick note on tool-calling again - structured outputs and function calling are supported; however, some open checkpoints need instruction-tuning to be robust for deterministic function invocation. We can help with a light fine-tune or recommend variants that are better at structured output.

[47:30] Maya Lin: Cost sensitivity - our CFO cares about dollar-per-1k tokens and predictable monthly cost. Can you provide committed pricing for Dedicated?
[47:40] Sofia Ramirez: Yes - committed reserved capacity pricing is standard for Dedicated. We'll put together a 6/12-month comparison for you.

[50:10] Raj Patel: Anything else?
[50:15] Sofia Ramirez: Recap - Redwood to: 1) send pricing and SOW template, 2) share SOC2/ISO + network and identity docs, 3) Daniel to run benchmark on Dedicated with Orion prompt set (benchmarks: latency p50/p95, accuracy per language, cost per 1k tokens), 4) Plan a 1-hour benchmark review week of 2027-12-27.
[50:40] Maya Lin: Sounds good, we'll upload prompts by Tuesday.
[50:45] Lea Ortiz: We'll compile compliance questions and share by Monday.
[50:50] Sofia Ramirez: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and add next steps in CRM.
[50:56] Raj Patel: Thanks all.
